what_it_asks_for: Tell the person they are dealing with an AI system
who_it_reaches: Providers of AI systems that interact directly with people — the Commission names chatbots, AI agents and avatars — wherever they are established, if the system is placed on the EU market, put into service in the EU, or its output is used in the EU.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach a system that runs only in the background, only machine to machine, or with no direct contact with people; and it does not reach a case where it is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person that they are dealing with an AI.
exact_quote: Providers of AI systems that directly interact with people must design and develop those systems in such a way that the individuals concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious.

what_it_asks_for: Show the notice from the start of the first interaction
who_it_reaches: The same providers as Article 50(1). The Commission says the notice comes at the start of the first interaction, clearly and distinguishably, and in line with accessibility requirements.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach a system whose AI nature is obvious, and it is not satisfied by a line buried in terms of service or a privacy policy.
exact_quote: People must be notified when they are interacting with an AI system from the start of the first interaction in a clear and distinguishable manner and in accordance with accessibility requirements.

what_it_asks_for: Mark generative AI output so a machine can detect it
who_it_reaches: Providers of generative AI systems: the outputs carry effective, reliable, robust and interoperable machine-readable marks.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach a deployer who only uses somebody else's system — this paragraph is written at the provider — and a visible sentence on the page is not a machine-readable mark.
exact_quote: Providers must also ensure that the outputs of their generative AI systems are marked with effective, reliable, robust and interoperable machine-readable marks that enable the outputs to be detected as generated or manipulated by AI systems.

what_it_asks_for: The one grace period, and the date it ends
who_it_reaches: Systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026, and only for the marking and detection duty: those comply from 2 December 2026.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not extend to any other Article 50 duty, and content generated before 2 August 2026 does not have to be labelled retroactively.
exact_quote: A limited grace period is envisaged only for AI systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 and only as regards the marking and detection obligation for AI-generated content

what_it_asks_for: Tell people when emotion recognition or biometric categorisation is used
who_it_reaches: Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems: they inform the people exposed to the system.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach a person using such a system in a personal, non-professional capacity, and it is a deployer duty, not a provider one.
exact_quote: deployers must ensure that they inform people when they use emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems

what_it_asks_for: Label deepfakes, and AI text published on matters of public interest
who_it_reaches: Deployers who generate or manipulate image, audio or video that is a deepfake, and those who publish AI-generated or manipulated text on matters of public interest without human review or editorial control. The label reaches the person on first exposure at the latest.
who_it_does_not_reach: The Commission says AI generation or manipulation that does not make content falsely appear authentic or truthful — background scenes, special effects, standard pre- and post-processing — is not likely to be caught; and published text that did go through human review or editorial control is outside the text half.
exact_quote: clearly label deepfakes and AI-generated or manipulated text published on matters of public interest without human review or editorial control

law: California Business and Professions Code § 17941(a) (the BOT Act)
what_it_asks_for: Disclose that a bot is a bot when it sells or influences a vote
who_it_reaches: A bot used to communicate or interact with a person in California online, with intent to mislead about its artificial identity, in order to incentivize a purchase or sale in a commercial transaction or to influence a vote in an election.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach a bot used for anything other than those two purposes — a support or FAQ bot that sells nothing and canvasses no vote is outside the section — and a person who discloses that it is a bot is not liable under it.
exact_quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to use a bot to communicate or interact with another person in California online, with the intent to mislead the other person about its artificial identity

law: California Business and Professions Code § 17941(b) (the BOT Act)
what_it_asks_for: The disclosure has to be clear, conspicuous and designed to inform
who_it_reaches: Any disclosure given to escape liability under § 17941(a): it is clear, conspicuous, and reasonably designed to inform the people the bot talks to that it is a bot.
who_it_does_not_reach: It sets no wording and no placement, so it does not tell you where the line must sit; and it is only in play where § 17941(a) is.
exact_quote: The disclosure required by this section shall be clear, conspicuous, and reasonably designed to inform persons with whom the bot communicates or interacts that it is a bot.

what_it_asks_for: Say the companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human
who_it_reaches: Operators of companion chatbots, where a reasonable person interacting with it would be misled into believing they are interacting with a human.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach a chatbot no reasonable person would take for a human, and the chapter is about companion chatbots rather than ordinary customer-support bots.
exact_quote: If a reasonable person interacting with a companion chatbot would be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human, an operator shall issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human.

what_it_asks_for: For a user the operator knows is a minor: say it is AI, and repeat every three hours
who_it_reaches: Operators of companion chatbots, for a user the operator knows is a minor: disclose the interaction is with artificial intelligence, and by default give a break reminder at least every three hours.
who_it_does_not_reach: It is written for users the operator KNOWS are minors, so it does not reach an adult user; the three-hour cadence is a default, not an absolute.
exact_quote: Disclose to the user that the user is interacting with artificial intelligence.

what_it_asks_for: Hold a self-harm crisis protocol and publish it
who_it_reaches: Operators of companion chatbots: the bot does not engage with users at all unless the operator maintains a crisis protocol, and the details of that protocol are published on the operator's website.
who_it_does_not_reach: This is a protocol and a published page, not a notice line — a disclosure sentence does not answer it.
exact_quote: An operator shall prevent a companion chatbot on its companion chatbot platform from engaging with users unless the operator maintains a protocol for preventing the production of suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm content to the user

law: California AI Transparency Act, Business and Professions Code § 22757.1(d) (SB 942 as amended by AB 853)
what_it_asks_for: The size test that decides whether this chapter reaches you at all
who_it_reaches: A person who creates, codes or otherwise produces a generative AI system with over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users that is publicly accessible inside California.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach a generative AI system under that monthly threshold, or one that is not publicly accessible in California; and the chapter does not apply at all to products offering exclusively non-user-generated video game, television, streaming, movie or interactive experiences.
exact_quote: means a person that creates, codes, or otherwise produces a generative artificial intelligence system that has over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users and is publicly accessible within the geographic boundaries of the state.

law: California AI Transparency Act, Business and Professions Code § 22757.3(a)
what_it_asks_for: Offer the user a visible “this is AI-generated” label
who_it_reaches: Covered providers, for image, video or audio content their generative AI system created or altered: the user is offered the option of a manifest disclosure that identifies the content as AI-generated, is clear and conspicuous, and is permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove.
who_it_does_not_reach: This is an option offered to the user, not a label the provider must stamp on everything; and it is written about image, video and audio rather than text.
exact_quote: A covered provider shall offer the user the option to include a manifest disclosure in image, video, or audio content, or content that is any combination thereof

law: California AI Transparency Act, Business and Professions Code § 22757.3(b)
what_it_asks_for: Embed hidden provenance data in AI-generated image, video and audio
who_it_reaches: Covered providers: a latent disclosure carrying the provider's name, the system name and version, the time and date of creation or alteration and a unique identifier, detectable by the provider's own detection tool.
who_it_does_not_reach: A visible sentence on a page does not answer this — it asks for data inside the file — and it is written about image, video and audio rather than text.
exact_quote: A covered provider shall include a latent disclosure in AI-generated image, video, or audio content, or content that is any combination thereof

law: California AI Transparency Act, Business and Professions Code § 22757.2(a)
what_it_asks_for: Publish a free AI detection tool
who_it_reaches: Covered providers: a publicly accessible detection tool, free to the user, that reports system provenance data and supports an application programming interface.
who_it_does_not_reach: It is a tool to build and host, not a notice to write; nothing in a notice pack answers it.
exact_quote: A covered provider shall make available an AI detection tool at no cost to the user

law: Colorado SB 24-205, repealed and reenacted by SB26-189
what_it_asks_for: The 2024 Colorado AI Act is not the rule to write a notice against
who_it_reaches: Nothing: the General Assembly's own summary of SB26-189 says the act repeals and reenacts the 2024 provisions with new requirements.
who_it_does_not_reach: A notice written to the 2024 Colorado AI Act text is written to provisions that were repealed and reenacted.
exact_quote: In 2024, the general assembly enacted Senate Bill 24-205, which created consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.

what_it_asks_for: Clear and conspicuous notice at the point of interaction with a covered ADMT
who_it_reaches: Deployers of an automated decision-making technology used to materially influence a consequential decision — education, employment, housing, financial or lending services, insurance, health care, or essential government services and public benefits.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach a technology that is not used to materially influence one of those listed consequential decisions, and specified entities are exempted to the extent they comply with other legal obligations.
from_when: see the date note on this row
exact_quote: The act establishes consumer notice requirements, mandating that deployers provide clear and conspicuous notice to consumers at the point of interaction with a covered ADMT.

what_it_asks_for: Plain-language description within 30 days of an adverse consequential decision
who_it_reaches: Deployers, after a covered ADMT makes a consequential decision that results in an adverse outcome for the consumer.
who_it_does_not_reach: It is not triggered by a decision with no adverse outcome, and the attorney general is directed to write rules clarifying these post-adverse-outcome disclosures by 1 January 2027.
exact_quote: within 30 days after the covered ADMT makes a consequential decision that results in an adverse outcome for the consumer

what_it_asks_for: Give the deployer technical documentation from 1 January 2027
who_it_reaches: Developers of a covered ADMT: intended uses, categories of training data, known limitations, and instructions for appropriate use and human review, plus notice of material updates.
who_it_does_not_reach: It is a developer-to-deployer document, not a consumer notice; a company that only deploys somebody else's technology is on the receiving end of it.
exact_quote: starting January 1, 2027, to provide a deployer of a covered ADMT (deployer) with technical documentation describing the covered ADMT

what_it_asks_for: Keep compliance records for at least three years
who_it_reaches: Both developers and deployers of a covered ADMT.
who_it_does_not_reach: It says nothing about what a consumer is shown; a notice does not answer a record-keeping duty.
from_when: see the date note on the notice row
exact_quote: Both developers and deployers are required to retain records necessary to demonstrate compliance with the act for at least 3 years.

what_it_asks_for: Consumers may request meaningful human review and reconsideration
who_it_reaches: Consumers, after a covered ADMT makes a consequential decision resulting in an adverse outcome; they may also request the personal data used and correction of factually incorrect data.
who_it_does_not_reach: It is a right the consumer exercises, not a line of notice text, so a notice pack can point at it but cannot satisfy it.
from_when: see the date note on the notice row
exact_quote: The act also grants consumers the right to request meaningful human review and reconsideration following a covered ADMT making a consequential decision resulting in an adverse outcome.

what_it_asks_for: Answer honestly when a consumer asks whether they are talking to AI
who_it_reaches: A supplier using generative AI to interact with an individual in connection with a consumer transaction, once that individual asks or otherwise prompts about whether AI is being used.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not require an unprompted notice in a consumer transaction: the duty runs when the individual asks, and the ask has to be a clear and unambiguous request.
exact_quote: A supplier that uses generative artificial intelligence to interact with an individual in connection with a consumer transaction shall disclose to the individual that the individual is interacting with generative artificial intelligence and not a human

what_it_asks_for: Regulated occupations: disclose prominently, up front
who_it_reaches: An individual providing services in a regulated occupation, where generative AI use in providing those services is a high-risk AI interaction: verbally at the start of a verbal interaction, and in writing before a written one.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach an occupation that is not regulated, or a use that is not a high-risk AI interaction.
exact_quote: prominently disclose when an individual receiving services is interacting with generative artificial intelligence in the provision of regulated services if the use of generative artificial intelligence constitutes a high-risk artificial intelligence interaction

what_it_asks_for: The safe harbour: disclose at the outset and throughout
who_it_reaches: A person whose generative AI clearly and conspicuously discloses, at the outset of the interaction and throughout it, that it is generative AI, is not human, or is an AI assistant.
who_it_does_not_reach: It removes an enforcement action under 13-75-103 and nothing else; it is not a safe harbour for any other state's rule or for the EU.
exact_quote: A person is not subject to an enforcement action for violating Section 13-75-103 if the person

what_it_asks_for: Tell the consumer they are not engaging with a human being
who_it_reaches: A person using an AI chatbot, or any other computer technology, to engage in trade and commerce with a consumer in a way that may mislead or deceive a reasonable consumer into believing they are engaging with a human being.
who_it_does_not_reach: It does not reach a use that could not mislead or deceive a reasonable consumer, and the duty falls away where the consumer is notified clearly and conspicuously.
from_when: see the date note on this row
exact_quote: A person may not use an artificial intelligence chatbot or any other computer technology to engage in trade and commerce with a consumer in a manner that may mislead or deceive a reasonable consumer into believing that the consumer is engaging with a human being
